title: A quarrel over an ass’s shadow
source_text: Ἐν μὲν τῷ πρώτῳ τῶν πρὸς τὴν ἀλαζόνα ἐπιγραφὴν Κέλσου. ἐπιγράψαντος ἀληθῆ λόγον τὸ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν αὐτῷ συνταχθὲν βιβλίον. ὡς προσέταξας. κατὰ δύναμιν. πιστότατε Ἀμβρόσιε, διειλήφαμεν τὸ προοίμιον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἑξῆς ἕκαστον τῶν εἰρημένων βασανίζοντες. ἕως κατελήξαμεν εἰς τὴν παρ᾿ αὐτῷ δημηγορίαν τοῦ Ἰουδαίου. πεπλασμένην γεγονέναι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ἐν δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ πρὸς ὅλα. ὡς οἷοί τ᾿ ἦμεν. ἀπαντήσαντες τὰ τῆς πρὸς ἡμᾶς. τοὺς διὰ Χριστοῦ πιστεύοντας τῷ θεῷ. δημηγορίας τοῦ παρ᾿ αὐτῷ Ἰουδαίου. τρίτον τοῦτον ἐνιστάμεθα λόγον, ἐν ᾧ πρόκειται ἀγωνίσασθαι πρὸς ἃ ἐκτίθεται ὡς ἀπὸ ἰδίου προσώπου. φησὶ δὴ ὅτι εὐηθέστατα ἐρίζουσι πρὸς ἀλλήλους χριστιανοὶ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι. καὶ λέγει μηδὲν διαφέρειν ἡμῶν τὸν πρὸς ἀλλήλους διάλογον περὶ Χριστοῦ τῆς κατὰ τὴν παροιμίαν καλουμένης ὄνου σκιᾶς μάχης· καὶ οἴεται μηδὲν σεμνὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίων καὶ Χριστιανῶν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ζητήσει. πιστευόντων μὲν ἀμφοτέρων ὅτι ἀπὸ θείου πνεύματος ἐπροφητεύθη τις ἐπιδημήσων σωτὴρ τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων οὐκέτι δ᾿ ὁμολογούντων περὶ τοῦ ἐληλυθέναι τὸν προφητευόμενον ἢ μή. Χριστιανοὶ μὲν γὰρ τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὡς κατὰ τὰ προφητευόμενα ἐληλυθότι πεπιστεύκαμεν· Ἰουδαίων δ᾿ οἱ πλεῖστοι τοσοῦτο δέουσι τοῦ πιστεύειν εἰς αὐτὸν. ὡς καὶ τοὺς μὲν κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν ἐκεῖνον ἐπιβεβουλευκέναι τῷ Ἰησοῦ τοὺς δὲ νῦν εὐδοκοῦντας τοῖς ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων κατ᾿ αὐτοῦ τετολμημένοις τότε κακηγορεῖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ὡς διά τινος γοητείας πλασάμενον ὅτι ἄρα εἴη ὁ ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν κηρυχθεὶς ἐπιδημήσειν. καλούμενος κατὰ τὰ Ἰουδαίων πάτρια Χριστός.
pass_a_gloss: In the first [book] of the [books] against the boastful (ἀλαζών) title (ἐπιγραφή) of Celsus, who entitled (ἐπιγράφω) ‘True Doctrine’ (ἀληθὴς λόγος) the book composed (συντάσσω) by him against us, as you ordered (προστάσσω), according to [our] power (κατὰ δύναμιν), most faithful (πιστότατος) Ambrose, we have gone through (διαλαμβάνω) his preface (προοίμιον) and, testing (βασανίζω) in order each of the things said, until we ended (καταλήγω) at the public speech (δημηγορία) of the Jew with him, fabricated (πλάσσω) against Jesus. In the second, having met (ἀπαντάω), as we were able, all the [points] of the speech of the Jew with him against us, those believing (πιστεύω) in God through Christ, we set about (ἐνίσταμαι) this third book (λόγος), in which it is set before [us] to contend (ἀγωνίζομαι) against what he sets out (ἐκτίθημι) as from his own person (πρόσωπον). He says then that most foolishly (εὐηθέστατα, from εὐήθης) Christians and Jews quarrel (ἐρίζω) with one another; and he says that our dialogue (διάλογος) with one another about Christ differs in nothing from the fight (μάχη) called in the proverb (παροιμία) ‘of the shadow (σκιά) of an ass (ὄνος)’; and he thinks there is nothing dignified (σεμνός) in the inquiry (ζήτησις) of Jews and Christians with one another, both believing that from a divine spirit (θεῖον πνεῦμα) it was prophesied (προφητεύω) that a certain saviour (σωτήρ) would sojourn (ἐπιδημέω) among the race (γένος) of men, but no longer agreeing (ὁμολογέω) about whether the one prophesied has come or not. For we Christians have believed in Jesus as having come according to the things prophesied; but of the Jews the most are so far from (τοσοῦτο δέουσι) believing in him that those at that time (καιρός) plotted (ἐπιβουλεύω) against Jesus, and those now, approving (εὐδοκέω) the things dared (τολμάω) by the Jews against him then, revile (κακηγορέω) Jesus, as having feigned (πλάσσω, middle) by some sorcery (γοητεία) that he was the one proclaimed (κηρύσσω) by the prophets as about to sojourn, called according to the ancestral [usages] (πάτρια) of the Jews Christ.
pass_b_english: In the first book of our reply to Celsus’s boastful title (for he entitled the book he composed against us The True Doctrine), we dealt, as you instructed, most faithful Ambrose, and as far as we were able, with his preface, and then tested each of his statements in turn, until we ended with the speech of the Jew that he has invented against Jesus. In the second book we met, as best we could, every point in the speech that his Jew makes against us who believe in God through Christ. Now we begin this third book, in which our task is to contend with what he sets out in his own person.

He says that “Christians and Jews quarrel with one another most foolishly,” and he says that our debate with one another about Christ is no different from what the proverb calls “a fight over the shadow of an ass.” He thinks there is nothing worthy of respect in the inquiry that Jews and Christians carry on with one another, since both believe that it was prophesied by a divine Spirit that a Saviour would come to dwell among the human race, but beyond that they do not agree on whether the one prophesied has come or not.

For we Christians have believed in Jesus as the one who came in accordance with the prophecies. But most of the Jews are so far from believing in him that those of that time plotted against Jesus, and those of the present day, approving what the Jews then dared against him, speak evil of Jesus, as though by some sorcery he had pretended to be the one whose coming the prophets proclaimed, who is called Christ in the ancestral usage of the Jews.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 1 (Koetschau 3.1). Ambrose is Origen’s patron, at whose request the work was written. The first report of Celsus (ὅτι εὐηθέστατα ἐρίζουσι πρὸς ἀλλήλους χριστιανοὶ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι) keeps a finite verb after ὅτι and reads as Celsus’s own wording, so it is set in quotation marks; the next clause is indirect (infinitive, with Origen’s ‘our’) and only the proverb phrase is marked as Celsus’s words; the rest of Celsus’s view (καὶ οἴεται … ἢ μή) is indirect and left unquoted. ‘The shadow of an ass’ is a Greek proverb for a pointless dispute (it appears, for example, in Plato, Phaedrus 260c and Aristophanes, Wasps 191); Celsus is not quoting either, so no inline source is given. ‘θεῖον πνεῦμα’ is capitalised as ‘a divine Spirit’ because both parties mean the Spirit of God who spoke through the prophets. ‘τοὺς διὰ Χριστοῦ πιστεύοντας τῷ θεῷ’ may echo 1 Peter 1:21 (‘who through him believe in God’); possible allusion only, not cited inline. ‘ἐπιδημήσειν’ (would come to dwell) is rendered by ‘whose coming the prophets proclaimed’ in the last sentence. ‘ὡς προσέταξας. κατὰ δύναμιν’: the staged punctuation splits these; read as two parentheses (‘as you instructed … as far as we were able’). ‘οὐκέτι δ᾿ ὁμολογούντων’ rendered ‘but beyond that they do not agree’ (οὐκέτι marks where agreement stops, not a past agreement). No LXX renumbering arises.
‘came to a close at’ (κατελήξαμεν εἰς) made ‘ended with’
‘nothing of dignity’ (μηδὲν σεμνόν) made ‘nothing worthy of respect’
‘no longer agree’ (οὐκέτι ὁμολογούντων) made ‘beyond that they do not agree’, so it no longer implies a former agreement
